designGate.prompt: Before writing code, sketch how you will track owned vs reserved inventory per user/item, and what a pending trade stores so accept and cancel can finish or unwind without scanning all balances. Name the reservation structure and the trade record.

parts.title: Inventory and propose (reserve)

hints.text: get must not return qty that is already locked in an open proposal. What two numbers do you need per (user, item)?
owned[user][item] and reserved[user][item]. available = owned - reserved. propose bumps reserved on both sides.
If the second reserve fails, undo the first — otherwise a failed propose leaks a lock on the buyer.

probes: What does get return while a proposal is open?
How do you avoid leaving a partial reservation if seller cannot cover?

parts.title: Accept and cancel

hints.text: accept moves owned amounts and clears reserved; cancel only clears reserved. What status prevents doing either twice?
Store legs as (from, to, item, qty). accept: owned[from]-=qty, owned[to]+=qty, reserved[from]-=qty.
Unknown id or status != pending -> ValueError for both accept and cancel.

probes: Walk through balances after accept on the worked example.
Why is double-accept an error rather than a no-op?

parts.title: Multi-leg propose_legs

hints.text: propose is two legs. propose_legs is N legs with the same reserve-all-or-none rule.
Reserve in order; on failure release in reverse. Reuse accept/cancel unchanged.
Implement propose via propose_legs so one code path owns reservations.

probes: What must be true after a failed propose_legs — any residual reserved qty?
How would you extend this to timeouts on pending trades?

criteria: failed propose / propose_legs leave no residual reservations
owned vs reserved split is explicit
propose reuses the same leg/reservation path as propose_legs
insufficient inventory and double-settle cases considered
stated what get returns under an open reservation

provenance.note: Rewritten to inventory / propose / accept / propose_legs arc (peak_question_bank itemexchange.py).
